title: Hotels with an Empire State Building view: which room to book
metaDescription: Three Manhattan hotels with Empire State Building view rooms, the exact room category to book at each, and the look-alike rooms to skip.
h1: Hotels with an Empire State Building view, and which room to book
dek: Three hotels in Manhattan. For each one we list the exact room categories sold with the view, and the look-alike rooms that are sold without it.
teaser: From a plain king room named for the view to suites that list it only in a view line.

alternatives.title: No view room? Try a rooftop
alternatives.text: Oyster names the rooftop bar at Hotel Metro for close views of the Empire State Building, and says it is only open seasonally. It is a shared space, not a room.

faq.q: Which New York hotels sell rooms with an Empire State Building view?
faq.a: Of the hotels we checked in October 2026: The Langham sells suites with Empire State View in the name, the Archer Hotel sells two Empire View rooms, and The Ritz-Carlton NoMad lists the building in the view line of its Madison Suite.

faq.q: Does every room at these hotels see the Empire State Building?
faq.a: No. At the Archer only the two Empire View categories are named for it, and at The Langham the Superior, Deluxe and plain Junior Suite categories do not name it. Book the exact category listed above.

faq.q: Is a Fifth Avenue or Midtown view the same as an Empire State Building view?
faq.a: No. The Langham describes its plain Junior Suite with views of Fifth Avenue and Midtown Manhattan, and sells the Empire State View suites as separate categories.
